title: Introduce cost-beacon: tenant profiler and adaptive batch-stride defaults
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation: Customers struggle to pick safe yet cost‑effective defaults for batching and caching across tenants with diverse request shapes. Large config surfaces (stride, max_batch_delay_ms, KV prefill hints, and quant profile selection) mean teams either overprovision latency targets or accept expensive per‑token costs. This PR introduces 'cost-beacon', a lightweight tenant profiler and adaptive default generator that observes a short bootstrap window for a tenant and suggests conservative batch-stride defaults, cache prefill hints, and a per-tenant quant profile candidate.

What this change does (high level): Implements a runtime component (cost-beacon) plus a small CLI/agent (costctl) to run a 1–5 minute sampling pass per tenant (or for a subset of requests) to: 1) estimate effective sequence-length distribution and concurrency footprint, 2) compute an adaptive batch stride (micro-batching stride) that balances latency SLO vs unit-cost for that tenant, 3) suggest KV/prefix cache prefill thresholds and TTL hints to reduce repeated prefix work, and 4) run a lightweight quant profile probe (quant-thermostat probe) that scores candidate quantization points on a tiny eval set to recommend a conservative quant profile for production rollout.

Implementation notes: The profiler runs as an opt-in sidecar in Dedicated/Private deployments and as an account-level sampler in Hosted. The runtime side includes: runtime/batcher/stride_scheduler.go (new scheduler that accepts adaptive stride overrides), runtime/cache/prefill_hint.go (hint propagation / telemetry tagging), components/cost-beacon/collector.go (sampling, sketching histograms, and tenant model), components/cost-beacon/strategy.go (heuristics that map signals to defaults), cli/costctl/probe.go (CLI for dry-run and dry-simulate), and docs/quickstarts/cost-beacon.md. Config surfaced to Console: suggested defaults and a confidence score. We intentionally keep the initial heuristics conservative (favoring latency for interactive tenants) and provide an automatic rollback window controlled by rollout policies.

Checklist: - [x] Sampling pipeline and TTL-limited sketches implemented - [x] Stride calculator + scheduler integration - [x] KV prefill hinting into runtime traces - [x] Small quant probe harness with per-tenant candidate scoring - [x] CLI (costctl) dry-run and apply flow - [x] Unit and integration tests + perf microbenchmarks - [x] Docs + console annotations - [x] Canary rollout plan + feature flag gating

Testing and validation: Unit tests for stride math, cache hint propagation, and quant probe scoring included. Integration test spins up a 2-GPU local harness and verifies that stride override yields expected latency/cost tradeoffs for three synthetic workloads (short-chat, long-composition, high-concurrency inference). Perf bench was run using benchmark-lab with tenant workloads; measured median token-cost reduction of 8–14% for chat-like tenants with unchanged 95th-percentile latency under the conservative profile. CI initially failed lint (gofmt) and a flakey bench test (BenchStrideScheduler) — both addressed in follow-ups and re-ran CI passing.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated behind acct-level flag and a Console toggle. 2) Internal canary: 5 tenants on Dedicated for 48h with telemetry dashboards (latency SLOs, unit-cost, cache hit-rate). 3) Gradual expansion to Hosted with default 'suggest' mode (no automatic apply) before enabling auto-apply for tenants that opt in.

Risk and mitigations: - Incorrect quant recommendation: probe uses a conservative penalty for any loss of output coherence; recommendations are advisory until explicitly accepted. - Over-aggressive batching: scheduler enforces latency SLO ceilings and automatically reduces stride on observing SLO erosion. - Telemetry cost: sampling window is limited and sketching uses low-memory summaries.

Related work: This complements prior autotune efforts (prefill/autotune) by focusing on a short-lived, tenant-specific bootstrap that produces high-confidence conservative defaults rather than complex long-running autotuners. Linear refs: ENG-3482 (profiler), PM-112 (productization).

How to validate locally: run `make dev-costbeacon` to start the sidecar sampler against local redwood runtime; `costctl probe --tenant-id=demo --dry-run` will print suggested stride/cache/quant with confidence and simulated cost delta.

Notes: This PR purposefully keeps the decision mapping white-box and human-readable so SEs can audit suggested defaults for enterprise customers. Future follow-ups will add model-based suggestion and multi-tenant cross-signal aggregation.

release_notes: Introduce cost-beacon (tenant profiler) and adaptive batch-stride defaults plus a conservative quant probe. Adds costctl CLI with dry-run and apply. Feature gated; default mode = suggest. Reduces token unit-cost for chatlike tenants in early tests by 8–14% while preserving latency SLOs.
summary: Adds a conservative tenant profiling component that recommends batch and cache defaults plus quant candidates; CLI and docs included, canary-ready.
